title: Rav Chiyya bar Amram
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Bekhorot 36b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.36b.22) he says: “Three permit the firstborn where there is no expert.” Hyman proposes that Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin speaks in the name of Rav Amram, as in [Yevamot 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.25b.8). Hyman reports this reading in Shitah Mekubbetzet as well.[^1]

notes.text: Bekhorot 36b has Rav Chiyya bar Amram; Yevamot 25b gives Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin reporting Rav Amram. Hyman's statement of what SHOULD READ remains an attributed textual correction, not a new father-son identification. The reported Shitah Mekubbetzet reading was not freshly collated.

[Bekhorot 36b:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.36b.22) also mentions a panel of three for dissolving vows. It is this second ruling that [Yevamot 25b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.25b.8) transmits through Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin in Rav Amram’s name.
